title: The commandment concerning the plates
summary: Nephi commands Jacob to write selected precious things on the small plates, preserve them, and pass them to his descendants; the people's history is to be recorded on other plates.

explicit_facts.text: Fifty-five years had passed since Lehi left Jerusalem when Nephi gave Jacob a commandment concerning the small plates.
Nephi commanded Jacob to write a few things he considered most precious on the plates and to touch only lightly on the people's history.
Nephi said the people's history would be engraved on his other plates, and commanded Jacob to preserve the small plates and pass them down through generations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob writing on small plates, with Nephi giving him the instruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and material of the plates, writing tools, clothing, and surroundings.

narration.text: fifty and five years had passed away

prohibited_inventions: Do not show Lehi or portray the departure from Jerusalem as occurring in this scene.

title: What Jacob is to record
summary: Jacob explains that sacred preaching, great revelation, and prophecy should be recorded; he says revelations and prophecy made Christ and his coming kingdom known to them.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob was instructed to engrave the heads of sacred preaching, great revelation, or prophecy on the plates and touch on them as much as possible for Christ's sake and their people's sake.
Through faith and great anxiety, things that would happen to their people had been made manifest to them.
They had many revelations and much prophecy, and knew of Christ and his kingdom, which should come.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown writing or reflecting as narration describes what he was commanded to preserve.
unspecified_visual_details: Any particular revelation, prophecy, or vision; the appearance of Christ or his kingdom.

narration.text: we knew of Christ and his kingdom, which should come.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The text reports revelations and prophecy but does not describe a visible revelation in this passage.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an undescribed vision or show Christ physically present.

title: Laboring to persuade the people
summary: Jacob says he and others labored among their people to persuade them to come unto Christ. He takes upon himself the commandment given by Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: They labored diligently among their people to persuade them to come unto Christ and partake of God's goodness.
Jacob wished that all would believe in Christ, view his death, suffer his cross, and bear the world's shame; he undertook to fulfill Nephi's commandment.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob teaching people in a gathering, without depicting the death of Christ as a present event.
unspecified_visual_details: The number and identities of listeners, the precise teaching setting, and any visual representation of Christ's death.

narration.text: I, Jacob, take it upon me to fulfil the commandment of my brother Nephi.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The references to Christ's death and cross are teaching, not a narrated present-time event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Christ's death or invent words spoken by Jacob.

title: Nephi anoints a ruler
summary: Nephi begins to grow old, sees that he must soon die, and anoints a man to be king and ruler over his people.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi began to be old and saw that he must soon die.
Nephi anointed a man to be king and ruler over his people, according to the reigns of the kings.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and the unnamed man may be shown together during the anointing.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and manner of anointing.

narration.text: Now Nephi began to be old, and he saw that he must soon die;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not name the man Nephi anointed.
prohibited_inventions: Do not give the man a name or invent anointing words or ritual details.

title: The people's remembrance of Nephi
summary: Jacob recalls the people's love for Nephi, his protection and labor for them, and their practice of calling subsequent rulers by numbered forms of his name.

explicit_facts.text: The people loved Nephi exceedingly; he had been a great protector, wielded Laban's sword in their defense, and labored for their welfare.
The people wished to retain Nephi's name in remembrance and called rulers who reigned in his stead second Nephi, third Nephi, and so forth, whatever their personal names.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A respectful group may be shown remembering Nephi; the text does not specify a particular ceremony or gathering.
unspecified_visual_details: Any memorial, ceremony, or specific act of defense; Laban's sword is mentioned but not described here.

narration.text: the people were desirous to retain in remembrance his name.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The defense and labor are reported past events, not a new present-tense action scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unspecified battle or memorial rite.

title: Nephi dies

explicit_facts.text: Nephi died.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown at the moment of death, without adding medical or ceremonial detail.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, circumstances, and manner of Nephi's death.

narration.text: And it came to pass that Nephi died.

prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the circumstances, cause, or manner of death.

title: Names for the people
summary: Jacob lists the names by which the people had been called, then says he will use Lamanites for those seeking to destroy Nephi's people and Nephites for those friendly to Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: Those who were not Lamanites were Nephites, though they were also called Nephites, Jacobites, Josephites, Zoramites, Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites.
Jacob says he will call those who seek to destroy Nephi's people Lamanites, and those friendly to Nephi Nephites or the people of Nephi.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown writing the explanation as narration.
unspecified_visual_details: The identities and appearance of individuals belonging to the named groups.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are Jacob's naming conventions in his record.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a conflict or imply that all people bearing one listed name shared a single allegiance beyond Jacob's stated distinction.

title: Pride and wicked practices
summary: Under the second king, the people of Nephi began to grow hard in their hearts, indulge somewhat in wicked practices, search much gold and silver, and become somewhat proud.

explicit_facts.text: The people of Nephi began to grow hard in their hearts and indulge somewhat in wicked practices under the reign of the second king.
The verse compares those practices to David of old desiring many wives and concubines, and mentions Solomon as his son.
The people began to search much gold and silver and became somewhat lifted up in pride.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People may be shown searching for gold and silver, without specifying how or where.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting, the people's appearances, and the manner of their search.

narration.text: began to search much gold and silver

doctrinal_or_story_notes: David and Solomon are mentioned as comparisons, not as people present at this time.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict David or Solomon as present, identify the unnamed second king, invent individual relationships, or specify a mining method.

title: Jacob teaches at the temple
summary: Jacob teaches the people in the temple after receiving his errand from the Lord. He and Joseph had been consecrated priests and teachers by Nephi, and Jacob describes their responsibility to teach diligently.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob gave the people these words as he taught them in the temple, having obtained his errand from the Lord.
Jacob and his brother Joseph had been consecrated priests and teachers of the people by Nephi.
They took responsibility before the Lord to teach God's word diligently, lest the people's sins be upon their own heads.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob may be shown teaching the people in the temple; Joseph may be present as a fellow priest and teacher.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and layout of the temple, the specific words taught, and the manner of consecration.

narration.text: we did magnify our office unto the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Jacob describes the responsibility of teaching; the text does not narrate a divine appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lord visibly or invent a consecration ceremony.
